Maya (Marketing): Hey @eng-runtime — quick ask for next week's webinar. We need a focused rerun to validate latency percentiles and warmup effects for three model variants. Can we get results by EOD tomorrow?

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Sure. What exact metrics + variants do you want to see? Aggregates only or raw samples too?

Maya (Marketing): Aggregated CSV (one row per request) + one raw-sample log (first ~1k lines). Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99, mean, stdev, cold-first-request vs steady-state, tokens/sec, gpu_util, error counts.

Tina (Product Ops): Models to compare: baseline fp16, int8 quantized, and a canary small-fp16. We need side-by-side numbers for the deck.

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Proposed run matrix:
- Variants: model-v2-fp16, model-v2-int8, model-v2-canary-fp16
- Payload mix: short 0.6 (<=32), mid 0.3 (~128), long 0.1 (~512)
- Warmup policy: 50 reqs per worker OR 60s, whichever first
- Batch behavior: support single-request + batching up to 8

Sahil (Eng Runtime): For stable p99 I'd prefer >=10k requests per variant (about 6k short / 3k mid / 1k long). Is that okay?

Maya (Marketing): Yes 10k/variant is fine. We'll only show p95/p99 externally but want p50/p90 internally.

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Deliverables I'll produce: payloads.jsonl (seeded), raw-sample.log (first 1k), aggregated.csv (one row per request), summary_table.csv (aggregated percentiles & means), methodology.txt, anomalies.md.

Maya (Marketing): Also, we need a quick sanity check: if quantized p99 > fp16 p99 by >20% we should flag it (and marketing may drop that claim). Call out any >20% deltas.

Sahil (Eng Runtime): Noted. Quick note: quantized variants often have higher variance on very long sequences; we'll flag that in anomalies.md.

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Please share the payload generation command so runs are reproducible.

Maya (Marketing): Use this snippet (seeded):
```
python tools/sample_payloads.py --seed 2026 --n 10000 \
  --distribution \"short:0.6,mid:0.3,long:0.1\" \
  --lengths \"short:8,mid:128,long:512\" --output payloads.jsonl
```
Use it as source-of-truth for the run.

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Running on the ci-runtime pool to avoid noisy neighbors. ETA ~2-3h per variant. Will post artifact when done.

eng-runtime-bot: job #bench-1729456780 queued on pool ci-runtime. ETA ~8h total.

eng-runtime-bot: job #bench-1729456780 started (owner: Lucas).

eng-runtime-bot: job #bench-1729456780 completed. artifact: s3://redwood-bench/1729456780/results.zip

Lucas (Eng Runtime): Uploaded results. Quick highlights: model-v2-int8 p99 = +11% vs fp16 (within the 20% gate), canary-fp16 p99 = +3%. Long-cohort shows higher tail variance; see anomalies.md for details. Files uploaded: payloads.jsonl, raw-sample.log, aggregated.csv, summary_table.csv, methodology.txt, anomalies.md.

Maya (Marketing): Got it, thanks. I'll pull summary_table.csv to craft the slide and will message if we need further breakdowns. Appreciate the fast turnaround! :rocket:
